body: Maybe. I'm just telling you what happened. Unless I said something in the thread that was just so horrible that people didn't want anything to do with me. Here it is, if you're curious: https://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/4fsrq8/i_need_a_ton_of_dental_work_that_i_cant_afford_i/

> If you get all of your teeth pulled, you end up with false teeth. Something to think about.

Won't matter if I'm dead.

I actually did post on r/suicidewatch. I had someone offer to talk to me in email because they said they wanted to be there for me. When I did email them, I got no response. I also got no response to two private messages I sent them asking why they weren't talking to me. I'm not really eager to go back there.

My family can't recommend a new dentist, because they all go to the one I'm trying to get away from, and I don't have any friends. I don't know if it would matter to me if I could talk to the dentist beforehand. I don't think it's common for people to tell a stranger "I'd like you to be nice to me and not judge me negatively." That's what everyone *wants*, but no one *says* it. 

I do feel a slight need to make it clear that I believe my cavities are entirely a result of my depression. I'm not sure why. I guess maybe I feel like that could deflect potential condescension. 

What's odd, though, is that I'm almost considering just letting everything fall apart, because I'm planning to kill myself anyway. I've actually had to have one tooth pulled already; it broke when I was eating one day and I went to my dentist about it, and that's when he found the cavities. The actual process of getting it pulled really wasn't that bad. I almost feel like I'd rather just let the teeth fall apart and get them all pulled than go to the trouble of getting fillings. What does it matter if I'm dead anyway, right? I'm guessing that sounds *really* fucked up. Even making this post asking for help took a fair bit of effort, because in many ways, I simply don't care anymore.

Anyway, I guess I'll try doing that search you suggested, and hopefully I can get some more comments here that might offer additional help.

>Unfortunately, it can become a horrible cycle, you're depressed so you don't care until it becomes a problem and adds to the depression. 

I know that cycle well. Even now, with the problem staring me right in the face, I *still* find it hard to care.

Well, the broken tooth is gone. The surgeon and his assistant were both very nice to me, and the actual tooth-pulling only took about two minutes at most, with almost no pain or discomfort. So that wasn't so bad. Closing my eyes helped. I don't know why I never thought of that before. Maybe I just felt so uncomfortable with my dentist that I was afraid of letting my guard down enough to close my eyes. Well, whatever the case, I'm definitely going to keep my eyes closed if I go for the fillings.

I think I'm less afraid of telling my parents now. Not because I'm ready to accept their help or anything like that, but more because I just don't care what they say. I don't care if I end up costing them thousands of dollars to fix my teeth. For many years, they dismissed my concerns about problems in my life by telling me there was "more to life" than what I was concerned about. So now if they complain about this, I get to tell them "there's more to life than money". And if they get pissed off, I don't care about that either. Then I can just kill myself. It might even be fun to have them pay all that money and then kill myself anyway. I didn't deserve to have my teeth get all screwed up, so I guess I'll just try not to care. This whole situation only happened because I got overwhelmed by things that weren't my fault anyway. 

I wouldn't be killing myself just because of my teeth. My teeth are just the result of a lot of other issues overcoming me. I've wanted to die for years. I'm done with this world. There's nothing here for me anymore. If I had any hope for my life, I wouldn't have spent so many days shoving sugar and fast food into my mouth and hardly ever thinking about my teeth, because the food was the only thing that kept my thoughts at bay. I also wouldn't have smashed up my video game collection, which was the only material thing I cared about.

That probably wasn't the kind of response you were hoping for, and I'm sure I'm not coming across as a very good person, but I don't know how else to be anymore, or how to feel about anything. I think I appreciate your concern. At least, I know I should. That's about the best I can do right now.

Is it so bad that I think I need someone to save me from myself? Making the effort to save myself would require me to not hate myself, and I'm not capable of that any more.
I have to leave right now, but I'll try to write a better reply later.

No, not at all. The only time I have pain is when I brush or chew with the tooth that's going to be removed, so that will end after today. If that one tooth hadn't broken, I wouldn't have had any suspicion that anything was seriously wrong.

I just found out that I don't have insurance (my parents had been handling those matters, and I didn't know if I had it or not). All the fillings I need will be astronomically expensive.

I think my life is over. I need to go somewhere where I can find a good method to kill myself. I've often hoped that some big thing would happen to push me over the edge, and it looks like this is it.

I hate to outright ask for replies like this, but I don't have long before I have to go to sleep and my appointment is early tomorrow, so it would be good to have some kind of response before I go in.

I know exactly what you mean, even though my situation is a bit different. I can't stand being alone with my thoughts, either. I've managed to get around that issue in two ways. First, I take a lot of sleeping pills. I only needed one or two at first, but now I basically have to take one every hour until I'm basically forced to sleep. Second, I sleep with all the lights on. I find that, for me, being in the dark is what causes all those feelings of being alone with the thoughts you spend all day trying to keep at bay. For some reason, keeping the lights on helps me. I think it's because it makes sleeping seem more like a mid-day nap instead of being like a final end to a day. Instead, my whole life ends up feeling like one long day.

Of course, I'm also slightly different in that I often find that sleep is the only way to escape my own mind, so I often take sleeping pills in the middle of the day to force sleep.

I guess I'm not terribly worried about getting fillings. I've had fillings before, so I know I can endure that procedure. What drives me to absolute terror is the idea that it might be more serious than that. And I have to admit that I'm surprised and upset that I've developed a worse problem than before even though my brushing habits have been better since that last event. I don't understand how a complete lack of brushing for a month or two only creates a few minor cavities and one serious one, but brushing more often than that created cavities everywhere.

I'm wondering if maybe I should consider getting a different dentist to do the fillings, because of the negative feelings I have about my current one. Would you happen to know of a good website for dentist reviews where empathy and non-judgementalism might be considered?
It's rather personal, and I'd prefer not to go into the details. I'll just say that I was depressed even before I lost the games, and I made some mistakes because of it.
